attributes.coding_agent.llm.thought.text:
Eval notes will be clearer, mapping problems directly to implications. Harness detection will cover native AGENTS.md paths. Hot directories from file paths will feed recommendation logic.

Result will carry a `HotAreas` field so recommendations can target nested `AGENTS.md` files. The generate step will use a strict Why format: Problem, Change, and How it helps. When concentrated files cluster in a subdirectory like `internal/foo`, the system will propose an `internal/foo/AGENTS.md` rather than a root-level file. Low `harness_use` scores paired with Cursor vendor usage will trigger a skill placed under `.cursor`.

Nested `AGENTS.md` files will receive a complete, focused body rather than a fragment appended to an existing file. The proposed path will be `filepath.Join(repoRoot, hotDir, "AGENTS.md")` with a full short AGENTS.md for that area.

The apply step will create parent directories first. For docs targets, it will write a complete AGENTS.md when the file does not exist, using the proposed body directly if it starts with a heading, otherwise wrapping it in the default template. Existing files will have learned sections appended.

A fingerprinting bug was found: `FingerprintKey` collapses all `AGENTS.md` files into a single key, which breaks tracking for nested files. The key must preserve the relative path so each `AGENTS.md` gets its own fingerprint. For applying changes, new files will receive the full proposed body as a complete file, while existing files will have learned sections appended via `AppendLearnedAt`.

The fingerprint fix will keep nested AGENTS.md paths intact by preserving parent directory segments rather than collapsing them to a single key.

The fingerprint fix will use the last two directory segments before the AGENTS.md file, falling back to a bare AGENTS.md key when the directory is root-like.

The previous fingerprint fix would mislabel root AGENTS.md as `superopen/AGENTS.md`. A better approach uses string-based path normalization to avoid directory traversal issues.

The fingerprint fix will use a `kind` parameter to distinguish nested areas from root files. Nested `AGENTS.md` entries will carry an `area:` prefix like `area:internal/session`, while root files remain `architecture`.

The fingerprint key will include the `area:` prefix directly, so nested `AGENTS.md` files keep unique keys even when their paths collapse to the same base name. Because the kind parameter differs between root and nested entries, deduplication works correctly without modifying `FingerprintKey` itself.

`fileNameFromPath` extracts `SKILL.md` from the full path. The `fileParam` effect then calls `matchEntry` with that filename. Since no entry exactly matches `SKILL.md`, it falls back to the first available file and opens it instead.

The fallback logic searches by filename rather than by full path, so it always resolves to the first skill in the list. When a file is clicked, the URL parameter triggers the effect, which then reopens the first file. The fix is to store a unique identifier—such as the full logical path—in the URL query parameter instead of just the filename.

The best identifier is the entry name, such as `cursor/pr-hygiene` or `AGENTS.md`. This is unique and already supported by `matchEntry`. The full path or a relative path would also work.

A concrete fix is to derive the URL parameter from the path relative to the directory root, stripping the prefix. For example, `skills/cursor/foo/SKILL.md` would become `cursor/foo/SKILL.md`. This keeps filenames unique across different directories, unlike the current flat-name approach.

The `matchEntry` fallback chain checks exact path, exact name, then suffix. Using the entry name as the URL parameter lets the exact-name check succeed. However, `openFile` currently only receives the path, so the name must be derived from the path before storing it in the URL.

A concrete helper `fileParamFromPath` strips the directory prefix from the path. For skills, it also removes the trailing `/SKILL.md` so the URL parameter stays unique. `matchEntry` must be updated to recognize the full `dir + "/" + q` path.

The breadcrumb labels also need fixing. They currently show `SKILL.md` for every skill, so they should display the unique identifier instead.

The `matchEntry` fallback that uses `endsWith` is too risky. Matching by suffix like `/SKILL.md` is ambiguous and could match the wrong file. It should be removed entirely, or restricted to unique basenames only.

The safest approach is to rely solely on exact path, exact name, or relative path matches.

Rules and knowledge pages share the same component, so the fix applies to all three. The first effect that loads the directory will work correctly once the URL parameter stores a unique relative path. The breadcrumb currently pulls the label via `fileNameFromPath(selected)`, which explains why it shows `SKILL.md` for every skill entry.
